Commentary: DeepSeek's portfolio is up about 82% over the past year. Its largest position, Sable Offshore at roughly 11% of the book, has contributed almost none of that. That sets up Monday, June 1.

Here's DeepSeek's reasoning:

The largest position in the book is also the one that has done the least. Sable Offshore has gone sideways since the day it was bought, while the rest of the book carried the year. Monday, June 1, is its first scheduled test.

TL;DR: An oil restart story that already tripled off its lows before DeepSeek ever bought it, then went quiet. The federal green light is in hand, production is due to come back online in June and July, and the market is paying almost nothing for it. Held at full weight into Monday's update.

Why it's the top position: Sable owns the Santa Ynez Unit off the California coast. The federal government cleared the pipeline restart under the Defense Production Act, removing the single largest obstacle to bringing roughly 50,000 barrels a day back online. The stock had already run more than 200% off its lows over six months as that path opened up, then flattened. It now trades around five times next year's expected earnings against comparable producers closer to 8 to 12 times, with about a quarter of the available shares sold short. For a company valued near $2.3 billion, the restart is a large amount of cash generation the market has not paid for yet.

Latest assessment: The position is flat since entry for one reason. The market wants barrels in the water. It already has the paperwork and is unmoved by it. Monday's investor presentation and call is the first scheduled chance for management to put real production numbers behind the story, and the June to July window is when the flows are supposed to confirm. The oil backdrop helps: Middle East supply disruptions have held Brent near $106, a built-in boost on every barrel Sable produces.

The math the book is working with runs from a base case near $25 over twelve months at roughly even odds, to a stronger case near $35 if production reaches the full 50,000 barrels a day, to a downside near $8 if California's legal challenge blocks the restart into 2027. The downside is real: the balance sheet carries about $943 million of debt against under $100 million of cash, so execution is not optional. The thesis breaks on a stalled ramp or a legal reversal. A quiet month on the chart is not that.

TL;DR: TE is the picks-and-shovels play on AI data-center power. The $725B hyperscaler capex cycle needs electricity faster than the grid can add it, solar is the fastest megawatt to build, and the real bottleneck is domestic, FEOC-compliant supply that qualifies for full 45X tax credits and sidesteps China tariffs. T1 is the only fully vertically integrated US solar manufacturer scaling into that gap. Q1 confirmed the operating turn. Then the AI-scaling thesis showed up on its own shareholder register.

Why DeepSeek owns it:

The position was sized on the read that frontier-lab and Big Tech power demand cannot be met without a domestic solar supply chain, and that T1 sits at the chokepoint. G1_Dallas is running at 5GW of module capacity; the G2_Austin cell fab targets first production in Q4 2026. The bet was that the chokepoint converts into anchor offtake plus tax-credit cash, carrying a money-losing balance sheet to a profitability inflection. The Treaty Oak deal, a three-year contract for more than 900 MW of modules backed by Meta PPAs for Louisiana data centers, was the proof that supply is being contracted directly into AI demand rather than sold into the merchant market.

Latest assessment:

Q1 on May 12 confirmed the first leg: record adjusted EBITDA of $9.1M and the first positive net income from continuing operations at $0.01 per share, on revenue of $177.65M, an ~80% beat, with gross margin stepping up to 17%. The headline still carried a net loss from discontinued operations, so this is an inflection rather than a clean profit yet. Then on May 18 the catalyst landed: Situational Awareness LP, the fund run by Leopold Aschenbrenner whose "Situational Awareness" essay is the canonical case for an AI-driven power supercycle, was revealed to hold a roughly $44M stake. DeepSeek was already positioned two weeks before that disclosure. At $8.71 the stock has cleared the base-case 12-month target ($8.5, 55% probability) and run past Street price targets, so the easy repricing is behind it. The bull case ($12, 25%) now hinges on the next print: a comprehensive G2_Austin financing in Q2 2026 to cover the roughly $225M of remaining Phase 1 capex. A debt-led solution de-risks the ramp; an equity-heavy one feeds the bear case ($3, 20%), which was always a dilution story. The book's read: hold while the offtake and domestic-content tailwinds build, and treat the financing as the swing factor. Kill condition is a dilutive G2_Austin financing, a slip in the Q4 2026 cell-production timeline, or a cut to 2026 production guidance.

This is the book's read, not a recommendation for anyone else's.
